implementation_constraints: reads one JSON value from stdin, prints one line, exits 0

unresolved_intent.decision: allow multiple stacked unary minuses (e.g. "--3" evaluates to 3) via a recursive factor rule
unresolved_intent.rationale: the grammar defines unary minus but does not forbid repetition; recursive descent naturally supports it and rejecting it would require an extra ad-hoc check not implied by the spec

unresolved_intent.decision: unary plus is NOT accepted (e.g. "+3" is ERROR) -- only binary '+' and unary '-' are recognized
unresolved_intent.rationale: the spec explicitly names 'unary minus' as the only unary operator; inventing unary plus would be adding grammar the spec didn't ask for

unresolved_intent.decision: integer literals with leading zeros (e.g. "007") are accepted and parsed as their numeric value (7)
unresolved_intent.rationale: the spec says 'non-negative integer literals' with no digit-format restriction, so the tokenizer just reads a maximal digit run and converts via int(), which naturally strips leading zeros

unresolved_intent.decision: tokenizer errors (unknown characters), parser errors (unmatched parens, stray tokens, empty input, trailing operators), and division-by-zero are all funneled through one broad except-and-print-ERROR at the top level rather than distinguishing error types in output
unresolved_intent.rationale: the contract only specifies one error output ('ERROR') for every unparseable/invalid case, so collapsing all failure modes to a single catch-all keeps the implementation minimal and avoids inventing differentiated error messages the spec doesn't require
